summary.text: Michael Dublin, a Green Party candidate and retired public school teacher, lost the November 3, 2026 election for U.S. Senate in North Carolina to Roy Cooper.
A Raleigh native and Marine Corps veteran, he ran for U.S. House as a Green Party candidate in 2024.

paragraphs.text: Dublin was born in Raleigh, North Carolina, graduated from Sanderson High School and served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1986 to 1988.
He earned an undergraduate degree from North Carolina State University in 1999.
According to his Ballotpedia survey, Dublin taught public school for 25 years, serving as language arts department chair at Carroll Middle School and North Garner Middle School, and recently retired.
He says he also volunteered for 24 years in prison ministry at the Johnston County correctional facility, and he co-chairs the Black Caucus of the North Carolina Green Party.
Dublin was the Green Party candidate for North Carolina's 2nd Congressional District in 2024, receiving 2.1% of the vote.
He said he ran on universal health care, a living wage, affordable housing, a Green New Deal and refusing corporate money.
He received 0.9% of the vote to Roy Cooper's 58.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
